weeks.title: The Principles of Good Design
weeks.overview:
Welcome back. Now that you understand the foundations of graphic design and have been introduced to the tools you will be using, it is time to begin understanding what makes a design work.

A good design is not created by randomly placing text, images, colours, and shapes on a canvas. The elements within a design need to work together intentionally to communicate a message clearly and create a specific visual experience. This week you will be introduced to some of the fundamental principles that guide how designers organize and arrange visual elements — composition, hierarchy, layout, and the relationship between the elements within a design.

The goal is not simply to memorize a list of rules. The goal is to begin developing an understanding of why certain design decisions work, and how designers use principles to create more intentional and effective visual communication.
weeks.objectives:
By the end of this week you should be able to:

1. Explain what composition is, and how the arrangement of elements affects a design.
2. Describe hierarchy, and how it guides a viewer's eye through a design in a deliberate order.
3. Understand layout and how the placement of elements shapes the way a design is read.
4. Explain the relationship between different visual elements, and why they need to work together rather than compete.
5. Apply design principles to make a design clearer, more organized and more effective at communicating its message.
6. Recognise why some designs feel balanced and intentional while others feel confusing or difficult to follow.

Today's goal is to begin developing your design eye. Pay attention not only to what the principles are, but also to how and why they are used.

lessons.title: Welcome Back — The Principles of Good Design
lessons.content:
Welcome back.

Now that you understand the foundations of graphic design and have been introduced to the tools you will be using, it is time to begin understanding what makes a design work.

A good design is not created by randomly placing text, images, colours, and shapes on a canvas. The elements within a design need to work together intentionally to communicate a message clearly and create a specific visual experience.

In today's lesson, you will be introduced to some of the fundamental principles that guide how designers organize and arrange visual elements.

You will begin to explore how composition, hierarchy, layout, and other design principles influence the way a design looks, feels, and communicates.

The goal is not simply to memorize a list of rules.

The goal is to begin developing an understanding of why certain design decisions work and how designers use principles to create more intentional and effective visual communication.

lessons.title: What You'll Learn Today
lessons.content:
Today, you will learn about the fundamental principles that contribute to effective graphic design, with particular attention to:

- Composition
- Hierarchy
- Layout
- The relationship between different visual elements
- How design principles can be applied to create clearer and more effective designs

Work through the lesson below, then watch the full video before moving on. The principles covered today will be applied directly in your design work as the course progresses.

lessons.title: Part 1 — The Principles of Good Design
lessons.content:
Design principles provide a framework for making intentional visual decisions.

They help designers understand how different elements can be organized and combined so that a design communicates its intended message effectively.

In this lesson, you will be introduced to several important principles of good design and begin to understand how they influence the way viewers see, interpret, and interact with a design.

A BRIEF OVERVIEW

The explanation above is only a summary of the topic. The full lesson goes deeper into the principles of good design and how they can be applied in practice.

You are required to watch the full lesson below before proceeding.

lessons.title: Today's Goal
lessons.content:
Today's goal is to begin developing your design eye.

By the end of today's lesson, you should have a better understanding of why certain designs feel organized, clear, balanced, and intentional, while others may feel confusing or difficult to follow.

Pay attention not only to what the principles are, but also to how and why they are used.

You will begin applying these principles directly in your design work as the course progresses.

lessons.title: Tuesday — Layout & Composition
lessons.content:
Welcome back.

Today, we continue building your understanding of design principles by focusing on two important aspects of visual design: layout and composition.

A design is made up of multiple visual elements, but simply having the right elements is not enough. How those elements are arranged on the canvas can determine how the viewer sees, understands, and interacts with the design.

In today's lesson, you will explore how designers organize visual elements within a composition and how different arrangements can influence the overall structure, flow, and clarity of a design.

lessons.title: What You'll Learn Today — Layout & Composition
lessons.content:
Today, you will learn about:

- Layout
- Composition
- Arrangement of visual elements
- Creating structure and visual flow
- How the placement of elements affects the overall design

Work through the lesson below, then watch the full video before moving on.

lessons.title: Part 1 — Layout & Composition
lessons.content:
Layout and composition are concerned with how the different elements of a design come together within a given space.

In this lesson, you will explore how designers make decisions about the placement, positioning, spacing, and relationship between different elements to create a structured and intentional composition.

You will also begin to understand how the arrangement of elements can guide the viewer's attention and influence the way information is perceived.

A BRIEF OVERVIEW

The explanation above is only a summary of the topic. The full lesson goes deeper into layout and composition and demonstrates how these concepts can be applied when creating designs.

You are required to watch the full lesson below and pay attention to how the concepts are demonstrated.

lessons.title: Tuesday's Goal
lessons.content:
Today's goal is to understand that where you place something is just as important as what you place.

By the end of today's lesson, you should have a clearer understanding of how layout and composition help create structure, organization, and visual flow within a design.

As you watch, pay attention to how the arrangement of elements changes the way a design feels and how easily the viewer can understand its message.
